title: control-hypothesis-notebook-oliver-2025
content:
Purpose: quick brain-dump of control hypotheses, potential evidence locations, open questions for SOC2 scoping. Informal — use as a running notebook; will extract formal mapping later.

Context / goal:
- We're scoping a Type 2 SOC2 for infra+platform surface (hosted API + Dedicated + Private control plane). Primary audit period target: Q4 2025.
- This doc is personal scratch: map controls -> plausible artifacts -> gaps. Not exhaustive.

High-level control areas I care about first:
1) Access management (SC-AC) — auth, MFA, admin separation
2) Change control & code promotion (SC-CH) — PR reviews, deploy approvals, release notes
3) Logging & monitoring (SC-LO) — retention, alerts, evidence streams
4) Key management & encryption (SC-KM) — KMS usage, rotation, HSM notes for Private deployments
5) Incident response & backups (SC-IR) — runbooks, tabletop exercises, backup restores
6) Vendor/third-party (SC-VP) — cloud providers, managed infra vendors

Control hypotheses (quick):
- AC-1: All human console access requires Okta SSO + enforced MFA. Evidence: Okta admin reports, identity provider config export, Slack SAML connection screenshot. Gap: historical SSO log exports older than 90 days may need retention.
- AC-2: Privileged admin roles are limited to a small list; role review performed quarterly. Evidence: IAM group membership CSV from HR sync; quarterly review notes in Confluence (page: Trust > Role Reviews). Gap: need signed attestation doc for Q3 2025 review.
- CH-1: Changes to serving-runtime and infra repos require 2 reviewers for prod-facing PRs; release gate uses GitLab protected branches + MR approvals. Evidence: MR history for core repos, protected branch policy screenshots, release checklist (gitlab MR templates). Gap: auto-merge windows / emergency bypass process needs documented approver list.
- LO-1: Application and platform logs are centrally ingested into ELK/Datadog with 1-year retention; alerts for 5xx spikes and anomaly detection exist. Evidence: Datadog monitor exports, S3 lifecycle policy, ELK index retention config. Gap: need to demonstrate tamper-resistance / log integrity — consider signing or storing hash snapshots in immutable store.
- KM-1: Customer keys for Private deployment can be integrated with customer KMS; Redwood uses AWS KMS for host-managed keys with CMK rotation policy of 1 year. Evidence: KMS key policy, rotation config, key usage logs in CloudTrail. Gap: HSM evidence for on-prem option — where to surface HSM module attestation docs?
- IR-1: Incident runbooks live in Confluence; pagers in PagerDuty, postmortems written to shared drive (trust-ops). Evidence: sample postmortem, PagerDuty escalation policies, tabletop calendar invites. Gap: need a formal incident response test log for last 12 months.

Where evidence likely lives (quick map):
- Identity / Access reports: Okta admin console exports (Confluence link TBD) + HR list (GDrive: hr/headcount-export-2025.csv)
- Code review & deploy: GitLab MR diffs, CI/CD pipeline artifacts (gitlab job logs), release-engineering/weekly-release-notes docs in shared_drives
- Logs & monitoring: datadog/exported-monitors-yyyy-mm.json (in observability folder), s3://redwood-logs/lifecycle-policy.txt (reference)
- KMS / encryption traces: AWS CloudTrail (console export), Confluence page: Security > KMS-design, private-deployments/hsm-readme (maybe in shared_drives)
- Incident evidence: postmortems in shared drive (customer-success and trust-ops), slack threads archived (#oncall-incidents)

Open questions to triage with infra/product owners:
- Q1: Retention windows: auditors often want 12 months of immutable logs; do we have immutable backups for critical logs beyond standard S3? (Ask infra-ops)
- Q2: Admin approval attestations: do we have signed quarterly role-review artifacts or just meeting notes? Need formalized sign-off checklist.
- Q3: Emergency deploy bypasses: what is the documented process and who is authorized? Link to runbook?
- Q4: Private on-prem HSM: do we collect attestation/cert of FIPS/HSM vendor? Who on infra team owns this vendor relationship?

Quick experiments / mitigations to reduce audit friction:
- Start exporting quarterly role-review CSV + signed Confluence page where managers attest to membership (small 1-pager template).
- Create an immutable-log snapshot job: monthly hash of critical ELK indices pushed to an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled (WIP ticket INFRA-5642).
- Draft an "Emergency Deploy Attestation" MR template that requires owner sign-off and post-facto audit note.

Concrete next steps (actionable):
- A1: Schedule 30m with @Priya (security lead) + @Marta (infra) — go over KMS and log retention plans. (Target: by 2025-09-01)
- A2: Populate Confluence page with role-review template and link to HR export. Owner: Oliver. (Target: 2025-08-20)
- A3: Identify 3 representative postmortems from last 12 months and copy to evidence folder. Owner: Marta. (Target: 2025-08-30)
- A4: Open JIRA: INFRA-5642 (immutable-log-hash) — prototype and capture design decisions.

Notes / heuristics for auditors (brainstorm):
- Keep evidence minimal but clear: auditors want to see a chain (policy -> execution -> artifact), not raw dumps. So prep: policy doc + signed attestation + log snippet + export job.
- Group artifacts by control owner rather than system — better for interviews.

Random thoughts / friction points:
- Private customers often ask for HSM proof; we need a standard vendor-attestation template to hand out.
- Sales asks for SOC2 sticker quickly; we should push for an interim "SOC2-in-progress" one-pager with expected timeline.

Reference links I grabbed / should validate:
- Confluence SOC2 home: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TRUST/SOC2-Prep
- Slack channel to check: #trust-ops, #infra-oncall
- Example MR: gitlab.com/redwood/infra/-/merge_requests/214

End-state checklist (draft):
- Policies written and signed: access, change mgmt, incident response, backups (Y/N)
- Evidence indexed in shared drive with control mapping table (owner + artifact + date)
- Quarterly reviews on calendar for role membership + change mgmt approvals
- At least 12 months of logs & postmortems available and accessible to auditor
- Immutable logging / hash snapshots documented and prototype completed

If I forget later: todo add a small section mapping Redwood product features to control owners e.g., Hosted-API: auth & rate-limit evidence lives with product-hosted-api; Dedicated: capacity/SLA ownership is infra-prod; Private: sales+solutions own HSM discussions.

Scratchpad footer: capture small phrases to copy into a formal mapping table later: 
- "policy -> evidence -> owner -> link -> sample-date"
- "signed quarterly attestation = control owner signature"
- "immutable-log-snapshots -> S3 Object Lock"

-- Oliver 

(ended as a messy notebook — will clean to Confluence after the triage meeting)
